slots.body:

slots.title: US close — Sept. 27, 2026
slots.body:
US equity indexes closed higher in the 2026-09-27 snapshot.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average led with a 0.9% gain to 51,828.62, up 478.64 points.
The S&P 500 rose 0.5% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% to 27,068.72.
The Russell 2000 was nearly flat, up 0.1% to 2,837.55.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 5.1% to 14.87, from a prior close of 15.67, while the major benchmarks finished in positive territory.

Microsoft was among the strongest megacaps in the dataset, up 3.7% to 516.17.
Apple rose 1.5% to 341.07, with a session high of 341.67 against a 52-week high of 345.34 in the quote fields.

Meta Platforms fell 3.3% to 751.66, the largest percentage decline among the listed megacaps.
Tesla slipped 1.5% to 372.11.
NVIDIA edged up 0.2% to 225.07 on heavy volume in the actives list.

Intel closed down 3.4% to 123.00 and appeared among the most active symbols.
Alibaba was down 0.8% to 109.74; Reuters reported that China could allow some domestic companies including Alibaba to buy a new Nvidia chip built for high-end professional computers.

Large US banks posted solid gains: JPMorgan Chase rose 1.3% to 343.06 and Bank of America rose 1.2% to 56.70.
Chevron and Exxon Mobil were lower, with $CVX down 0.6% to 204.44 and $XOM down 1.0% to 160.56.

Gold futures in the cross-asset block fell 2.1% to 4,229.60.
The United States Oil Fund proxy was down 3.1% to 148.33, while Brent crude in the commodity fields rose 1.7% to 106.14.

Bitcoin USD was down 1.2% to 83,420.10 in the same snapshot.
The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund proxy slipped 0.2% to 28.62.

Treasury yield levels in the injected curve (dated 2026-09-25) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and a 2s–10s spread of 0.36 percentage points.
No sector performance breakdown or US economic release was included in this payload, and the earnings calendar array was empty.

Overseas index fields in the file included the Hang Seng up 0.7% to 24,679.00 and the FTSE 100 up 0.1% to 10,695.25; the Nikkei 225 quote showed a flat 0.0% change to 66,333.53.

Weekend headlines in the news feed included China describing a two-month extension of a US trade truce as room to advance talks, and coverage of the Trump–Xi summit noting limited deliverables and planned formal discussion of AI risks.
